questions.text: A healthcare provider uses generative AI to create personalized patient summaries based on medical records. The AI system adjusts its outputs based on the specifics of each case. Which generative AI advantage is demonstrated here?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Adaptability

The key advantage of generative AI demonstrated in this scenario is adaptability. The AI system is able to adjust its outputs based on the specifics of each patient case, meaning it can process various types of input data (medical records) and generate personalized summaries accordingly. This adaptability allows the AI to tailor its outputs to different contexts and needs, providing a highly flexible solution for complex tasks like patient care. In healthcare, where each patient‘s case can differ significantly, the ability to generate unique, personalized summaries is a major strength of generative AI, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of healthcare delivery.

Incorrect

High manual effort

Generative AI is designed to reduce manual effort by automating content creation. In this case, it is doing the opposite of requiring high manual effort, as it adjusts its outputs automatically based on the data provided.

Fixed responses

The AI is demonstrating the opposite of fixed responses. It is flexible and adaptable, providing customized summaries based on individual patient records. Fixed responses would limit the AI's usefulness in this context.

Complexity of implementation

While generative AI systems can be complex to implement, this scenario emphasizes the AI‘s ability to adapt to different patient cases, rather than focusing on the complexity of setup or maintenance.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/generative-ai

questions.text: Your team needs a machine learning model for image recognition but lacks the resources to build one from scratch. Your team lead suggests using an existing model that has been trained on millions of images and can be fine-tuned for your specific use case. What type of model should you use?

options.text: Supervised learning model built from scratch

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Open-source pre-trained model

In this scenario, where your team lacks the resources to build a machine learning model from scratch but needs a model for image recognition, the best option is to use an open-source pre-trained model. Pre-trained models are machine learning models that have been trained on large datasets, such as millions of images, to recognize general patterns. These models can be fine-tuned (through transfer learning) for specific use cases, saving time, effort, and computational resources. Open-source pre-trained models are widely available and accessible through libraries like TensorFlow Hub, PyTorch Hub, or AWS SageMaker JumpStart. By using a pre-trained model, you benefit from the model‘s ability to recognize common features, like edges or textures, while focusing on adapting it to your specific needs, such as recognizing particular objects relevant to your domain.

Incorrect

Custom model trained from scratch

Training a custom model from scratch involves gathering data, defining the architecture, and training the model, which is resource-intensive. It is not ideal when resources are limited, especially for image recognition tasks, which require large datasets and significant computational power.

Reinforcement learning model

Reinforcement learning involves training models based on reward systems and is typically used for tasks like robotics or game playing, not for image recognition. It's not suitable in this context where an image recognition model is needed.

Supervised learning model built from scratch

While supervised learning is suitable for image recognition, building a model from scratch in this case would require significant resources. It is not efficient compared to using a pre-trained model, especially when existing models can be fine-tuned for the task at hand.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/solutions/machine-learning/pre-trained-models

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/studio-jumpstart.html

questions.text: Your company is using a large foundation model to generate marketing content, but the model occasionally produces factually incorrect statements (hallucinations). To improve the model‘s reliability, which method should you prioritize?

options.text: Reducing the number of layers in the transformer model
Fine-tuning the model with reinforcement learning
Incorporating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve factual information
Increasing the token count to capture more context

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Incorporating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve factual information

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique where the model retrieves relevant, factual information from external sources (such as a knowledge base or database) during the generation process. This helps reduce the occurrence of hallucinations by grounding the model‘s output in factual data. In marketing content generation, where accuracy is critical, RAG ensures that the model generates information based on reliable sources rather than producing incorrect or fabricated content. By integrating this method, the model becomes more reliable, as it supplements its generative capabilities with real-time factual retrieval.

Incorrect

Increasing the token count to capture more context

While increasing the token count may help the model capture more context, it does not directly address the issue of hallucinations. More context can improve coherence but doesn't ensure factual accuracy.

Fine-tuning the model with reinforcement learning

Fine-tuning with reinforcement learning can improve model performance on specific tasks, but it doesn't directly focus on reducing factual inaccuracies or hallucinations.

Reducing the number of layers in the transformer model

Reducing the number of layers may simplify the model but can potentially harm performance. It does not help mitigate hallucinations or improve factual reliability.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation

questions.text: A company wants to build an AI system to analyze customer feedback from social media in real time. The team needs to classify the feedback into categories like positive, negative, or neutral. Which AI/ML technique is most appropriate for this scenario?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Classification

Classification is the most appropriate AI/ML technique for categorizing customer feedback into predefined categories such as positive, negative, or neutral. In this context, classification models are trained on labeled datasets where the feedback is already categorized, enabling the model to learn and predict the correct category for new, unseen feedback. Sentiment analysis, which is a common task in natural language processing (NLP), often uses classification models to determine whether a piece of text is expressing a positive, negative, or neutral sentiment.

Incorrect

Clustering

Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique that groups data into clusters based on similarity. It is not appropriate for this task because clustering does not rely on predefined categories like positive, negative, or neutral, and is typically used for discovering natural groupings in data.

Regression

Regression is used for predicting continuous values (e.g., sales predictions, stock prices) and is not suitable for categorizing feedback into discrete categories such as positive, negative, or neutral.

Dimensionality reduction

Dimensionality reduction is a technique used to reduce the number of input variables in a dataset. While useful for simplifying data, it is not a technique for classifying text into categories.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/types-of-ml-models.html

questions.text: A research team is tasked with building a language model that can understand and generate medical reports. They plan to use a pre-trained foundation model trained on general text data. However, they need the model to specifically excel in medical terminology and contexts. Which of the following processes should they apply to adapt the model for medical-specific tasks?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Fine-tuning with medical data

Fine-tuning is a process in machine learning where a pre-trained model is further trained on a smaller, task-specific dataset to improve performance in a particular domain. It allows the model to adapt to new tasks or data while leveraging the knowledge from its original training.

Fine-tuning a pre-trained foundation model with domain-specific medical data is the most effective way to adapt the model for medical terminology and contexts. This process involves taking a model that has already learned general linguistic patterns and further training it on specialized datasets that contain medical terms, phrases, and structures. Fine-tuning allows the model to retain its general understanding of language while becoming highly proficient in the medical domain. This approach is efficient because it builds on existing knowledge rather than starting from scratch, making it ideal for adapting models to specific tasks like understanding and generating medical reports.

Incorrect

Continuous pre-training with medical data

Continuous pre-training focuses on extending the training of the foundation model with additional data, but it is less effective for task-specific adaptation. Fine-tuning is better for ensuring the model excels in a specialized field like medicine.

Instruction tuning with general text

Instruction tuning involves training a model to follow instructions across different tasks, but using general text for this process won‘t help the model excel in the medical domain. Fine-tuning with medical-specific data is more appropriate for the goal of adapting to medical reports.

Pre-training from scratch

Pre-training from scratch requires extensive computational resources and data, and it would not leverage the benefits of using a pre-trained foundation model. Fine-tuning is a much more efficient process for this situation.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-foundation-models-fine-tuning.html

questions.text: You are tasked with setting up an AI system that requires strict control over access to sensitive data, ensuring only authorized personnel can access the data. What is the best approach to secure data access?

options.text: Monitor data access using AWS Glue.
Use Amazon Transcribe to log access attempts.
Implement IAM roles, policies, and permissions to control access.
Encrypt the data but do not set any specific access permissions.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Implement IAM roles, policies, and permissions to control access.

Implementing IAM (Identity and Access Management) roles, policies, and permissions is the best approach to secure data access in AWS. IAM allows you to create and manage AWS users and groups and use permissions to allow or deny their access to AWS resources. By defining specific roles and attaching policies that grant precise permissions, you ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data. IAM policies can be tailored to grant the least privilege necessary, reducing the risk of unauthorized access. This method provides a robust and flexible way to control access, audit user actions, and comply with security best practices and regulatory requirements. It also integrates seamlessly with other AWS services, making it a comprehensive solution for securing data in your AI system.

Incorrect

Use Amazon Transcribe to log access attempts.

Amazon Transcribe is a speech-to-text service and is not designed for logging access attempts. It does not provide functionality for monitoring or controlling data access.

Encrypt the data but do not set any specific access permissions.

Encrypting data is important for security, but without proper access permissions, unauthorized users may still access or attempt to decrypt the data. Encryption should be combined with access controls for full protection.

Monitor data access using AWS Glue.

AWS Glue is a data integration service used for ETL (extract, transform, load) processes, not for monitoring data access. It doesn‘t provide mechanisms to control or monitor who accesses data.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html

questions.text: Your team is designing a foundation model application that requires high interpretability of the model's decision-making process. However, foundation models like transformers can be seen as black boxes. Which technique would help improve transparency and interpretability?

options.text: Applying post-hoc interpretability techniques such as SHAP or LIME
Increasing the number of tokens used during training
Fine-tuning the model with human feedback

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Applying post-hoc interpretability techniques such as SHAP or LIME

Post-hoc interpretability techniques, like SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) or LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), are designed to help make models more transparent after training. These techniques analyze the model‘s predictions to provide explanations about how different features contributed to the decision-making process. For foundation models, which are often considered “black boxes,“ applying SHAP or LIME can reveal insights into why a model made a particular decision. This is especially important in cases where interpretability is crucial, such as in healthcare, finance, or any domain requiring trust in the model‘s outputs. These methods do not change the model itself but offer a way to understand its predictions.

Incorrect

Fine-tuning the model with human feedback

Fine-tuning with human feedback helps improve the model's performance and alignment with human values but does not directly enhance interpretability. It's aimed at refining output quality rather than explaining how the model makes decisions.

Using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

RAG enhances the model by retrieving relevant external knowledge to improve responses but does not focus on making the decision-making process more transparent or interpretable.

Increasing the number of tokens used during training

Increasing the number of tokens during training might improve the model‘s performance or understanding of data, but it does not address the issue of interpretability.

questions.text: A company is developing a mobile application that uses image recognition to identify products from photos. The application must run smoothly on various devices, including low-power smartphones, without consuming too many resources. What should be the primary selection criterion when choosing a pre-trained model for this application? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Model size

For a mobile application running on a wide range of devices, including low-power smartphones, the size of the model is a crucial factor. Smaller models typically consume fewer resources such as memory and processing power, allowing the app to run smoothly on devices with limited capabilities. A large model may provide high accuracy but could strain the device's resources, leading to slower performance or even making the app unusable on lower-end smartphones. Therefore, choosing a model that balances size and accuracy is essential for mobile deployment.

Latency

Latency is another critical consideration for mobile applications, particularly for real-time tasks like image recognition. Users expect immediate responses when interacting with apps, so a model with low latency is crucial to ensure smooth performance. High latency could lead to delays in identifying products, which would negatively impact the user experience. The model must be able to quickly process images and return results without excessive delay, especially on devices with limited processing power.

Incorrect

Cost of fine-tuning

While cost can be a factor in model selection, it is not as critical in this scenario as performance on low-power devices and smooth user experience. The primary concerns here are the model‘s ability to run efficiently on mobile hardware.

Multi-lingual support

Multi-lingual support is irrelevant for an image recognition application. This feature is more relevant for tasks like language translation or text analysis but has no direct impact on image-based product recognition.

Input/output length

Input/output length refers to tasks involving sequences, such as natural language processing, but is not directly applicable to image recognition tasks in mobile apps.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/mobile/mobile-application-development

questions.text: You are working with a client that wants to integrate AI-driven text-to-speech capabilities into their customer service system. They have strict performance and scalability requirements. Which AWS service would be the most appropriate to implement?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Polly

Amazon Polly converts text into natural-sounding speech. It uses advanced deep learning technologies to synthesize lifelike voices, making it ideal for AI-driven text-to-speech applications. Polly supports multiple languages and voice styles, allowing businesses to enhance customer experiences.

For a client looking to integrate AI-driven text-to-speech capabilities with strict performance and scalability requirements, Amazon Polly is the best choice. It allows users to convert text in real-time or batch processes, scales easily based on demand, and provides high-quality, natural speech synthesis. Polly is well-suited for customer service systems that need to handle large volumes of text-to-speech conversions without performance degradation.

Incorrect

Amazon SageMaker

Amazon SageMaker is a service for building, training, and deploying machine learning models. While powerful for AI development, it is not specifically designed for text-to-speech tasks. SageMaker is better suited for creating custom models, not for integrating pre-built text-to-speech solutions like Polly.

Amazon Transcribe

Amazon Transcribe is used for converting speech to text (speech recognition). It's the opposite of what the client needs for text-to-speech capabilities. This service is useful for transcription purposes but not for creating speech from text input.

Amazon Rekognition

Amazon Rekognition is used for image and video analysis, such as object detection and facial recognition. It does not provide text-to-speech functionalities, making it unsuitable for this use case.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/what-is.html

questions.text: You are building a generative AI chatbot and need it to perform well in multiple tasks, such as answering questions and generating summaries. Which concept allows the model to process different modalities like text, images, and speech?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Multi-modal Models

Multi-modal Models are designed to process and generate data across different modalities, such as text, images, and speech. In the context of a generative AI chatbot, multi-modal models allow the chatbot to handle various input types (e.g., text questions, image analysis, or speech input) and produce appropriate outputs for these different types of data. These models can combine information from different sources and are often used in tasks like visual question answering, image captioning, or speech-to-text generation. Multi-modal models enable the chatbot to perform well across a range of tasks by leveraging diverse data types.

Incorrect

Sequence-to-Sequence Models

Sequence-to-sequence models are typically used for tasks like translation or text summarization, where an input sequence (e.g., a sentence) is transformed into an output sequence. While useful for text-based tasks, they are not designed to handle multiple data modalities.

Tokenization

Tokenization is the process of converting text into smaller units (tokens) for processing by a model, but it doesn't handle different modalities like images or speech.

Chain-of-Thought Prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting is a method used to improve reasoning by breaking down complex problems into intermediate steps. It is useful for improving text-based reasoning but doesn't handle multiple data types (modalities).

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/generative-ai-and-multi-modal-agents-in-aws-the-key-to-unlocking-new-value-in-financial-markets

questions.text: You are tasked with developing a transparent and explainable AI system for healthcare diagnoses. The stakeholders demand the ability to explain how predictions are made, especially for critical life-or-death decisions. What approach should you take to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to document model transparency.
Avoid using any explainable AI tools to simplify development.
Focus on improving the model's performance without worrying about interpretability.
Use a black-box model to enhance accuracy, even if it‘s less transparent.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Use Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to document model transparency.

Using Amazon SageMaker Model Cards is a practical approach to develop a transparent and explainable AI system in healthcare. Model Cards help you document critical details about your machine learning models, including their intended use cases, limitations, training data, and performance metrics. This comprehensive documentation provides stakeholders with a clear understanding of how predictions are made, which is essential for critical life-or-death decisions. By making the model‘s inner workings transparent, you ensure that healthcare professionals can trust and effectively interpret the AI‘s recommendations. This aligns with the stakeholders‘ demands for explainability and supports compliance with regulatory requirements in the healthcare industry.

Incorrect

Focus on improving the model's performance without worrying about interpretability.

Focusing solely on performance while ignoring interpretability neglects the stakeholders‘ need for explainability. In healthcare, understanding how a model arrives at a decision is as important as the decision itself.

Use a black-box model to enhance accuracy, even if it‘s less transparent.

Using a black-box model sacrifices transparency for accuracy. Stakeholders require insight into the decision-making process, so a less transparent model does not meet their needs.

Avoid using any explainable AI tools to simplify development.

Avoiding explainable AI tools may simplify development but fails to address the critical requirement of model explainability demanded by stakeholders.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-cards.html

questions.text: Your organization has developed a pre-trained foundation model for language translation but requires better accuracy in translating industry-specific jargon. You need to fine-tune the model using specific documents in your domain. What data preparation strategy is essential for this fine-tuning process?

options.text: Randomly selecting data samples without quality checks
Labeling the data with domain-specific terms
Using only pre-trained general models without data curation
Curation of a diverse general-purpose dataset

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Labeling the data with domain-specific terms

When fine-tuning a pre-trained foundation model for language translation in a specific domain, it is crucial to label the data with industry-specific terms. This strategy ensures that the model learns the relevant jargon and terminologies used in the specific industry, thereby improving its accuracy in translating documents. Fine-tuning with labeled domain-specific data allows the model to adapt its general language knowledge to specialized contexts, ensuring more precise translations in areas like medical, financial, or legal industries where accuracy is critical.

Incorrect

Curation of a diverse general-purpose dataset

A diverse general-purpose dataset is useful for building models that can handle a wide range of tasks, but in this scenario, it will not address the need for industry-specific terminology and jargon, which is essential for achieving accuracy in translations.

Using only pre-trained general models without data curation

While using a pre-trained model is beneficial, fine-tuning with domain-specific data is critical to improving performance for specialized tasks. Without data curation, the model will lack the precision needed to translate industry-specific terms.

Randomly selecting data samples without quality checks

Randomly selecting data without ensuring its relevance or quality would negatively affect the model's performance. In this case, fine-tuning requires carefully curated and labeled data that accurately represents industry-specific terminology.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/multi-model-endpoints.html

questions.text: You are leading a project to implement a machine learning model that processes personally identifiable information (PII) of users. To ensure compliance with data privacy laws like GDPR, you need a tool to automatically identify and categorize sensitive data stored in your AWS environment. Which AWS service would you use to detect and manage sensitive data in your AI solution?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Macie

Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and privacy service that uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data, such as personally identifiable information (PII) stored in your AWS environment. It is particularly useful for ensuring compliance with data privacy laws such as GDPR by continuously monitoring and reporting on sensitive data across your storage solutions, such as Amazon S3 buckets. With Amazon Macie, you can identify where PII is located, understand how it's being accessed, and apply proper controls to ensure that your AI solution adheres to privacy regulations. This makes it an ideal choice for managing sensitive data in a machine learning project where compliance is critical.

Incorrect

AWS Artifact

AWS Artifact is a repository of compliance-related reports and documentation provided by AWS. While it helps with accessing AWS compliance certifications and agreements, it does not actively identify or manage sensitive data in your environment.

AWS Trusted Advisor

AWS Trusted Advisor is a tool that provides recommendations to help optimize your AWS environment for cost, security, and performance. However, it does not specialize in identifying or managing sensitive data such as PII.

Amazon S3

Amazon S3 is a scalable storage service for storing and retrieving data. While it allows you to store sensitive data, it does not detect or classify PII.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html

questions.text: A healthcare company is interested in using AI to improve its diagnostics. They have a large dataset of medical images, and they want the AI system to assist doctors in diagnosing diseases. What type of AI/ML solution would be most suitable for this application?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Computer Vision

Computer Vision is the most suitable AI/ML solution for analyzing medical images to assist doctors in diagnosing diseases. This field involves enabling computers to interpret and understand visual information from the world, much like human vision. In healthcare, computer vision algorithms can process large volumes of medical images such as X-rays, MRIs, CT scans, and ultrasound images to detect anomalies or patterns indicative of specific medical conditions. Techniques like convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are commonly used to recognize intricate features within images that may be imperceptible to the human eye. By using computer vision, healthcare providers can achieve faster and more accurate diagnostics, reduce human error, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. The automation of image analysis also allows doctors to focus more on patient care rather than time-consuming image examinations.

Incorrect

Natural Language Processing

Natural Language Processing (NLP) focuses on the interaction between computers and human language, enabling machines to understand, interpret, and generate human language. While NLP is valuable for analyzing textual data like medical records or patient notes, it is not suited for processing and interpreting medical images for diagnostic purposes.

Recommendation Systems

Recommendation systems are designed to suggest products, services, or information to users based on data analysis of user behavior and preferences. They are commonly used in e-commerce and content platforms but are not applicable to analyzing medical images for disease diagnosis.

Regression Analysis

Regression Analysis is a statistical method used to model the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables. While it can be used for predictive analytics in healthcare (e.g., predicting patient readmission rates), it is not suitable for interpreting complex visual data found in medical images.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/computer-vision

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/what-is.html

questions.text: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using generative AI models in production environments?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Hallucinations and non-determinism

One of the major disadvantages of using generative AI models is the potential for hallucinations and non-determinism. Hallucinations occur when the model generates outputs that are plausible but factually incorrect or nonsensical. Non-determinism means that the model can produce different outputs for the same input across different runs, making it harder to ensure consistent responses. These behaviors can be problematic in environments that require reliable, predictable, and accurate outputs, such as customer service or legal applications. Addressing these issues often requires additional model tuning and monitoring in production.

Incorrect

High interpretability and explainability

Generative AI models generally lack high interpretability and explainability. Understanding how they generate specific outputs is difficult, as their internal workings involve complex neural networks and layers. This makes it hard to track or explain why certain decisions are made.

Scalability and adaptability

Generative AI models are known for being highly scalable and adaptable. Once trained, they can easily be scaled across various use cases or integrated into different applications, which is generally considered an advantage, not a disadvantage.

Simplicity of implementation

While generative AI models can be complex to develop and fine-tune, many frameworks and platforms (like AWS SageMaker) make their implementation relatively straightforward. This is more of an advantage than a disadvantage, as users can leverage pre-built models and services.

Summarization

In this scenario, the model is designed to generate short summaries of long legal documents, enabling lawyers to quickly review the key points. Summarization is a common application of generative AI, particularly in natural language processing (NLP), where the model distills lengthy text into concise, relevant summaries while preserving important information. This use case is highly beneficial for professionals dealing with large volumes of text, such as legal documents, where quick comprehension of content is crucial.

Code Generation

Code generation refers to using AI to automatically generate programming code from high-level specifications or natural language inputs, which is unrelated to summarizing legal documents.

Image Generation

Image generation involves creating images based on input data or prompts, which is not relevant in this case, where the focus is on generating text summaries.

Customer Service Agents

While AI can be used for customer service agents to automate responses or assist with queries, this use case is more focused on document summarization for legal professionals, not customer support.

questions.text: Your company is developing a custom recommendation system using a foundation model. You are deciding between pre-training a model from scratch or fine-tuning an existing pre-trained model. The project has strict budget constraints. Which of the following best explains the cost tradeoff between pre-training and fine-tuning?

options.text: Fine-tuning is more costly in the long run due to higher maintenance needs, while pre-training has lower overall costs.
Pre-training is more cost-effective for small datasets, while fine-tuning requires more resources.
Pre-training offers more customization flexibility at a lower cost than fine-tuning.
Pre-training is more expensive and time-consuming, while fine-tuning a pre-trained model offers a more affordable and faster option.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Pre-training is more expensive and time-consuming, while fine-tuning a pre-trained model offers a more affordable and faster option.

Pre-training a model from scratch involves training on a large-scale dataset and requires significant computational resources, time, and expertise. This makes it a costly process, especially when strict budget constraints are in place. In contrast, fine-tuning a pre-trained model allows you to leverage the general knowledge already acquired by the model and adjust it to your specific use case. This process is much faster and requires fewer resources, making it a more affordable option. Fine-tuning is especially cost-effective when dealing with domain-specific tasks, as it minimizes the need for large datasets and extensive training.

Incorrect

Pre-training is more cost-effective for small datasets, while fine-tuning requires more resources.

Pre-training is computationally expensive regardless of dataset size because it typically requires large datasets and significant resources to build a foundation model from scratch. Fine-tuning is less resource-intensive, even for smaller datasets.

Fine-tuning is more costly in the long run due to higher maintenance needs, while pre-training has lower overall costs.

Fine-tuning generally incurs lower long-term costs compared to pre-training. Pre-training requires substantial initial investment, and once fine-tuned, the model tends to require less frequent updates, keeping operational costs lower.

Pre-training offers more customization flexibility at a lower cost than fine-tuning.

While pre-training allows for greater control and customization, it is significantly more expensive and time-consuming than fine-tuning. Fine-tuning strikes a balance between customization and cost.

questions.text: A company has implemented a generative AI model to automate customer support responses. After deployment, the AI frequently generates incorrect or misleading answers, resulting in customer dissatisfaction. What practice could have prevented this issue?

options.text: Ensuring the model is environmentally sustainable.
Monitoring the model with tools like Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect and fix issues like hallucinations.
Providing fewer training examples to simplify the model.
Ignoring customer complaints and focusing on model accuracy.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Monitoring the model with tools like Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect and fix issues like hallucinations.

Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors the quality of machine learning models deployed in production. It automatically detects data drift, bias, and anomalies by comparing incoming data with training datasets. SageMaker Model Monitor helps ensure that models remain accurate over time, even as the data changes, by triggering alerts when deviations occur. It supports features like explainability and logging, making it easier to diagnose issues and improve model performance. Users can create custom monitoring schedules and set up remediation workflows, ensuring real-time insights into model health.

By using monitoring tools like Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor, the company can continuously keep an eye on the AI model‘s performance after deployment. This practice helps in detecting issues such as hallucinations, where the model generates incorrect or misleading information. Early detection allows the team to address these problems promptly by adjusting the model, updating training data, or fine-tuning parameters. Continuous monitoring ensures that AI provides accurate and reliable responses, leading to better customer satisfaction and trust.

Incorrect

Providing fewer training examples to simplify the model.

Using fewer training examples can actually weaken the model‘s ability to generate accurate responses, as it may not learn enough from limited data.

Ensuring the model is environmentally sustainable.

While sustainability is important, it doesn‘t directly affect the model‘s tendency to produce incorrect or misleading answers.

Ignoring customer complaints and focusing on model accuracy.

Ignoring customer complaints is detrimental. Customer feedback is valuable for identifying issues with the model‘s performance that need to be addressed.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor.html

questions.text: You are tasked with building a recommendation system using a pre-trained foundation model. To improve the model's performance for your specific use case, which technique would be most appropriate for tailoring the pre-trained model to your dataset?

options.text: Fine-tuning the model on domain-specific data

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Fine-tuning the model on domain-specific data

Fine-tuning a pre-trained model on domain-specific data is the most appropriate technique for improving the model‘s performance for your specific use case. Fine-tuning involves taking a model that has already been trained on a large, general dataset and adjusting its parameters by training it further on a smaller, specialized dataset that reflects the unique needs of your application. This allows the model to learn patterns and nuances relevant to your dataset, making it more accurate and effective for tasks like recommendation systems in a particular domain (e.g., retail, media, or healthcare).

Incorrect

Pre-training the model from scratch

Pre-training a model from scratch is resource-intensive and time-consuming. It‘s not necessary if you already have a pre-trained foundation model, as fine-tuning is a more efficient method to adapt the model to your specific use case.

Zero-shot learning

Zero-shot learning enables models to make predictions on tasks they haven‘t been explicitly trained for, but it's not as effective for improving performance on a domain-specific task as fine-tuning with relevant data.

Token augmentation

Token augmentation refers to techniques that enhance data by adding variations at the token level (words or subwords). While useful in some contexts, it's not as effective as fine-tuning a model for improving recommendation system performance.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-foundation-models-fine-tuning.html

questions.text: A company is developing an AI-powered writing assistant that helps users generate business emails. The system needs to see examples of professional emails to learn how to structure them properly. They provide a few example emails in the prompt to guide the model. Which prompt engineering technique are they using?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting is a technique where the model is provided with a few examples in the prompt to guide its understanding of how to perform a specific task. In this scenario, the company is giving the AI-powered writing assistant several examples of professional emails to help it learn how to structure new emails. These examples serve as reference points, enabling the model to generate business emails in a similar format and style. Few-shot prompting is effective for tasks where you want the model to mimic the structure, tone, or style demonstrated in the provided examples, making it an appropriate technique in this case.

Incorrect

Zero-shot prompting

Zero-shot prompting involves asking the model to perform a task without providing any examples or context. Since the company is giving examples to guide the AI, this is not zero-shot prompting.

Chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting is used to help the model break down complex problems into intermediate steps before arriving at a solution. This is not relevant to the task of generating business emails based on examples.

Prompt templates

Prompt templates provide a fixed structure or format that the model follows, but they do not involve showing examples. In this case, the focus is on providing example emails, which is a different approach from using templates.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/implementing-advanced-prompt-engineering-with-amazon-bedrock

questions.text: A business wants to generate real-time insights from unstructured text data such as customer reviews and support tickets. Which AWS service would you recommend for sentiment analysis?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Comprehend

Amazon Comprehend uses natural language processing (NLP) to analyze unstructured text data. It can identify the sentiment (positive, negative, neutral, or mixed) from customer reviews, support tickets, social media posts, and more. By using Amazon Comprehend, businesses can gain real-time insights into customer opinions, which helps in improving customer experience, enhancing products, and optimizing customer support processes. Additionally, Amazon Comprehend can extract key phrases, entities, and topics, making it a versatile tool for text analysis. This makes it ideal for applications that need sentiment analysis and other text comprehension tasks.

Incorrect

Amazon Transcribe

Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. It is primarily used for transcription tasks, such as converting audio into text. It does not perform sentiment analysis but can be used alongside other services like Amazon Comprehend for text analytics.

Amazon Lex

Amazon Lex is an AWS service for building conversational interfaces like chatbots and voice assistants. While it helps in understanding speech and text, it is not specifically designed for sentiment analysis of text data like customer reviews.

Amazon Kendra

Amazon Kendra is an intelligent search service that uses machine learning to provide more relevant search results. It is optimized for search queries within an organization‘s content but does not focus on sentiment analysis.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/what-is.html

questions.text: A company is developing an AI system that is still under development, and the developer team has noticed vulnerabilities related to external data injections during the prompt generation phase. What security concern should be addressed to protect the system from malicious input?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Prompt injection attacks

The concern of prompt injection attacks should be addressed to protect the AI system from malicious input during the prompt generation phase. Prompt injection attacks occur when external actors inject harmful or manipulated inputs that can alter the behavior of the AI system, potentially causing it to generate incorrect or inappropriate outputs. These attacks exploit the generative nature of the AI by introducing data that the system interprets and acts upon, possibly leading to unintended or harmful consequences. To mitigate these risks, developers can implement input validation, sanitization processes, and security checks to ensure that only appropriate and safe prompts are processed by the AI system. Additionally, monitoring and logging input data can help detect and respond to potential injection attacks.

Incorrect

Access control policies

While access control policies are essential for securing any system by ensuring that only authorized users can access specific resources, they do not directly address the risk of prompt injection attacks. Access controls protect against unauthorized access to the system but do not prevent authorized users or external interfaces from introducing harmful inputs once they have legitimate access.

Encryption at rest

Encryption at rest is a security measure that protects data stored on disk by converting it into an unreadable form for anyone who does not have the decryption key. While it is crucial for protecting data from unauthorized access or theft, encryption at rest does not prevent prompt injection attacks because it does not address the security of data in transit or being processed.

Data compression

Data compression involves reducing the size of data to save storage space or decrease transmission time. While useful for efficiency, data compression does not contribute to security against prompt injection attacks. It is unrelated to the specific security measures needed to guard against the manipulation of input data in AI systems.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/llm-prompt-engineering-best-practices/common-attacks.html

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between AI and machine learning (ML)? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AI is a specific field within ML focused on image and speech recognition.
AI only involves rule-based decision systems, while ML involves learning algorithms.
AI systems are limited to supervised learning models, whereas ML uses various learning techniques.
ML is a subset of AI that focuses on using data to improve predictions over time.
AI refers to a broader concept of creating intelligent machines, whereas ML specifically refers to systems that learn from data.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

ML is a subset of AI that focuses on using data to improve predictions over time.

Machine learning is a specialized area within the broader field of AI, and its primary goal is to enable systems to learn from data and improve their predictions or decisions over time without explicit programming. ML techniques such as supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning help systems identify patterns and make decisions based on past experiences.

AI refers to a broader concept of creating intelligent machines, whereas ML specifically refers to systems that learn from data.

AI encompasses a wide range of approaches aimed at creating intelligent systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as problem-solving, decision-making, and perception. Machine learning is a subset of AI that focuses specifically on learning from data to enhance task performance, distinguishing it from rule-based AI systems.

Incorrect

AI is a specific field within ML focused on image and speech recognition.

This is incorrect because AI is the overarching field, and ML is a subset of it. While image and speech recognition are common applications of AI and ML, AI is not a subfield of ML.

AI only involves rule-based decision systems, while ML involves learning algorithms.

While AI can include rule-based systems (like expert systems), it is not limited to them. AI also includes learning algorithms, which are covered by ML techniques.

AI systems are limited to supervised learning models, whereas ML uses various learning techniques.

This is incorrect because AI is not limited to supervised learning. AI includes a wide range of methods, while ML itself uses various techniques, including supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/artificial-intelligence

https://aws.amazon.com/ai/machine-learning

questions.text: A retail company wants to use AI/ML to predict future sales trends. They have historical sales data and want the system to automatically adjust based on new inputs over time. What type of inferencing is best suited for this use case? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanationHtml:
• Incorrect Supervised Inferencing
    • Typically used when your data has labeled examples (input → known output).
    • Example: Predicting whether a customer will churn (yes/no) based on features.
    • Problem: Sales forecasting is time-series prediction, not classic classification/regression with static labels.
  • Correct Predictive Inferencing
    • This refers to making predictions on future outcomes using a trained model.
    • In AWS context, “predictive” is aligned with forecasting future values, which is exactly what sales forecasting is.
  • Incorrect Batch Inferencing
    • Processes large datasets in bulk, not necessarily in real time.
    • Could be used for running forecasts across many products at once, but doesn’t cover the automatic adjustment over time requirement.
  • Correct Real-time Inferencing
    • Used when predictions need to happen immediately as new data arrives.
    • For a system that adjusts automatically as new inputs arrive, this is suitable.
  • Incorrect Manual Inferencing
    • Predictions are triggered manually, not automatic.
    • Not suitable for automatic adjustment.

questions.text: Your company is developing an AI model, you need to ensure that the data used is governed according to compliance protocols and that proper access control is enforced to prevent unauthorized use. Which of the following strategies is best for data governance?

options.text: Implement AWS Shared Responsibility Model for governance
Store data without logging to increase system speed
Use public data without monitoring to avoid complexity
Apply logging, retention, and monitoring for data lifecycle management

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Apply logging, retention, and monitoring for data lifecycle management

    • Effective data governance requires visibility and control over how data is stored, accessed, and used.
    • Logging ensures auditability (who accessed what, when).
    • Retention policies enforce compliance with regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA).
    • Monitoring ensures ongoing oversight to detect unauthorized access or misuse.
    • This aligns directly with AWS best practices for data lifecycle management and governance.

Incorrect

Implement AWS Shared Responsibility Model for governance

    • The Shared Responsibility Model defines security responsibilities between AWS and the customer.
    • It is a conceptual framework, not a direct governance strategy.
    • While important to understand, it does not itself enforce compliance protocols or access control.

Store data without logging to increase system speed

    • Disabling logging sacrifices auditability and compliance.
    • Speed gains are irrelevant compared to the risk of unauthorized access and lack of accountability.
    • This violates governance principles.

Use public data without monitoring to avoid complexity

    • Even public data requires governance if used in AI models (bias, compliance, licensing).
    • Avoiding monitoring increases risk of data misuse and non-compliance.
    • Governance is about control and oversight, not reducing complexity at the expense of security.

questions.text: After deploying a foundation model for a recommendation system, your team is actively monitoring user feedback and making updates to improve the model. What stage of the foundation model lifecycle involves incorporating this user feedback into future model versions?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Fine-tuning

  • Correct because fine-tuning is the stage where feedback and new data are incorporated into the foundation model to improve its accuracy and relevance.
  • In this scenario, user feedback is used to adjust the model’s parameters or retrain it on updated datasets, ensuring the recommendation system evolves with user needs.
  • Fine-tuning is the lifecycle step that bridges deployment with continuous improvement.

Incorrect

Evaluation

  • Incorrect because evaluation refers to testing and validating the model’s performance against benchmarks or datasets.
  • While evaluation may highlight issues, it does not directly involve incorporating user feedback into future versions.

Feedback

  • Incorrect because feedback is an input to the process, not a formal stage in the foundation model lifecycle.
  • The lifecycle emphasizes structured stages like pre-training, fine-tuning, and evaluation, rather than “feedback” as a standalone stage.

Pre-training

  • Incorrect because pre-training is the initial stage where the foundation model is trained on large, general-purpose datasets.
  • It occurs before deployment and does not involve user feedback from real-world usage.

questions.text: A company wants to implement an AI solution to detect fraudulent transactions in real-time. Which of the following use cases could benefit the most from using AI/ML? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Fraud detection using real-time transaction analysis
Perform sentiment analysis on customer support transcripts
Assist human decision-making in transaction validation
Automation of simple tasks with no variability
Predict future market trends based on historical data

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Fraud detection using real-time transaction analysis

  • Correct because fraud detection is a classic AI/ML use case.
  • Machine learning models can analyze transaction patterns in real-time, detect anomalies, and flag suspicious activity faster than rule-based systems.
  • This directly aligns with the company’s goal of preventing fraudulent transactions.

Assist human decision-making in transaction validation

  • Correct because AI/ML can provide decision support by scoring transactions based on risk.
  • Instead of replacing humans, AI augments analysts by prioritizing which transactions need review.
  • This reduces workload and improves accuracy in fraud prevention.

Incorrect

Perform sentiment analysis on customer support transcripts

  • Incorrect because sentiment analysis is useful for customer experience insights, not fraud detection.
  • It does not address the company’s need for real-time transaction monitoring.

Automation of simple tasks with no variability

  • Incorrect because tasks with no variability do not require AI/ML.
  • Simple automation (scripts, RPA) is sufficient; AI adds no value here.

Predict future market trends based on historical data

  • Incorrect because market trend prediction is a forecasting use case, not related to detecting fraudulent transactions.
  • While valuable, it does not solve the company’s immediate fraud detection requirement.

questions.text: You are working for a company that wants to build a conversational AI system using a foundation model. The team needs to select a pre-trained model, and one of the main requirements is multilingual support as the chatbot will interact with customers in multiple languages. Cost efficiency is also a concern for the project. Which approach should you take to select the appropriate foundation model on Amazon Bedrock for this project?

options.text: Pick any model from Amazon Bedrock and rely on manual translations for any unsupported languages.
Select a foundation model that supports multilingual capabilities and customize it through fine-tuning or in-context learning to improve cost-efficiency.
Choose a foundation model based solely on its size, ensuring the model with the largest parameter count is selected for higher performance.
Use a model that performs best for English and translate the responses to other languages using Amazon Translate.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Select a foundation model that supports multilingual capabilities and customize it through fine-tuning or in-context learning to improve cost-efficiency. This is correct because Amazon Bedrock provides access to multiple foundation models, some of which are optimized for multilingual support. Choosing a model that inherently supports multiple languages ensures the chatbot can interact with diverse customers. Fine-tuning or using in-context learning allows tailoring the model to the company’s specific needs without retraining from scratch, which improves cost efficiency.

Incorrect

Pick any model from Amazon Bedrock and rely on manual translations for any unsupported languages. Incorrect because relying on manual translations introduces inefficiency, increases costs, and reduces scalability. It defeats the purpose of using a multilingual foundation model.

Choose a foundation model based solely on its size, ensuring the model with the largest parameter count is selected for higher performance. Incorrect because larger models are not always cost-efficient. They may provide higher performance but at significantly higher computational and financial costs. The requirement here emphasizes multilingual support and cost efficiency, not just raw size.

Use a model that performs best for English and translate the responses to other languages using Amazon Translate. Incorrect because while Amazon Translate can handle multilingual responses, this approach adds complexity and cost. It also risks losing conversational context during translation. A multilingual foundation model is more efficient and accurate for this use case.

questions.text: You are using a generative AI model to create artwork for a marketing campaign. A competitor claims that some of the generated images resemble copyrighted works. What is the legal risk in this situation?

options.text: You can avoid legal risks by simply attributing the images to the AI model in use.
The model could produce outputs that infringe on existing copyrighted works, leading to intellectual property infringement claims.
The AI-generated images are unique and protected under fair use, so there is no legal risk.
Since AI models generate content autonomously, the responsibility for legal risks falls solely on the model provider.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

The model could produce outputs that infringe on existing copyrighted works, leading to intellectual property infringement claims.

The primary legal risk in this scenario arises from the possibility that the AI-generated images may closely resemble or replicate elements of existing copyrighted works. Generative AI models are trained on vast amounts of data, which may include copyrighted material. While the AI generates new content, it can sometimes unintentionally produce outputs that closely resemble existing copyrighted works. This can lead to potential intellectual property (IP) infringement claims, especially if the images bear substantial similarity to protected works. The organization using the AI-generated content may be held responsible for infringing on others‘ IP, even if the model generated the content autonomously. To mitigate this risk, businesses should consider legal reviews, use clear licensing models, or ensure that the data used to train the model is free from copyrighted material.

Incorrect

The AI-generated images are unique and protected under fair use, so there is no legal risk.

Fair use is a complex legal doctrine that does not automatically apply to AI-generated works. The mere fact that an AI generated the image does not guarantee that it qualifies as fair use, especially if it closely resembles copyrighted works.

Since AI models generate content autonomously, the responsibility for legal risks falls solely on the model provider.

Although model providers may share some liability, the user of the AI-generated content is often considered responsible for how the content is used, especially in commercial settings like marketing.

You can avoid legal risks by simply attributing the images to the AI model in use.

Attribution to the AI model alone does not absolve legal risks related to intellectual property infringement. Proper licensing or ensuring the content doesn‘t infringe on copyrighted works is more critical.

questions.text: You are developing a machine learning model to assist in making loan approval decisions for a financial institution. The institution‘s legal team is concerned about ensuring fairness and avoiding biases in the decision-making process. They have requested a model that can clearly explain its decision for each loan application. Which type of model would best suit this requirement?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Decision tree model

A decision tree model is inherently transparent and explainable. Decision trees work by making a series of logical decisions based on input features, which can be easily visualized and understood. Each decision in the tree corresponds to a specific rule that leads to the final prediction, making it straightforward to explain how a loan approval decision was made. This model's interpretability allows both the financial institution and its legal team to clearly understand the rationale behind each loan decision, ensuring fairness and avoiding biases. Given the need for transparency in high-stakes environments like financial institutions, decision trees provide the clarity necessary for regulatory compliance and trust in AI-driven decisions.

Incorrect

Neural network model

Neural networks are often seen as black-box models because they are complex and difficult to interpret. Their decision-making process is less transparent, making them less suited for situations where explainability is a key requirement.

Support vector machine (SVM)

SVMs are effective for certain tasks but are not inherently interpretable. They make decisions based on mathematical boundaries, which can be difficult to explain in a way that satisfies legal or regulatory needs for transparency.

Reinforcement learning model

Reinforcement learning models are complex and focus on learning optimal actions through trial and error. They are not typically used for tasks that require easy-to-understand, explainable decisions, making them unsuitable for this scenario.

questions.text: Your team is experimenting with generative AI and needs a sandbox environment to test various models, iterate quickly, and visualize the outputs. Which AWS tool provides an interactive environment for testing generative AI models?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

PartyRock, an Amazon Bedrock Playground

PartyRock is an Amazon Bedrock Playground designed for teams to experiment with generative AI models. This interactive environment allows developers to quickly iterate on models, visualize the outputs, and experiment with various configurations. PartyRock provides a user-friendly interface where users can test different foundational models (FMs), experiment with fine-tuning, and see how model outputs change based on input variations. The goal of this tool is to give teams a safe, isolated space (a “sandbox“) to iterate on model development without affecting production environments. It is especially valuable for testing new generative AI models, as it provides immediate feedback and insight into how models behave in real-world scenarios.

Incorrect

Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

While Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides access to pre-built machine learning models, including some generative AI models, it is more focused on productionizing ML workflows than on interactive testing in a sandbox environment like PartyRock.

Amazon Bedrock

Amazon Bedrock underpins the ability to build and deploy generative AI applications using foundational models, but it is not itself an interactive playground or sandbox. Bedrock provides the infrastructure, while PartyRock serves as the interactive environment.

Amazon Comprehend

Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing (NLP) service that helps extract insights from text data. It is not designed for testing or visualizing generative AI models, making it unsuitable for this use case.

References:

https://partyrock.aws

questions.text: You are tasked with building a specialized NLP model for a customer service chatbot. You need the model to handle domain-specific queries, but you want to minimize costs while still providing accurate responses. You are considering fine-tuning a pre-trained model on your specific dataset. What is a potential cost tradeoff of using fine-tuning in this scenario?

options.text: Increased costs due to the need for large training datasets
Moderate one-time customization costs and lower operational costs
Low initial costs but higher long-term maintenance costs
High compute costs for retraining the entire model

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Moderate one-time customization costs and lower operational costs

Fine-tuning a pre-trained model allows you to adapt an existing NLP model to your specific domain without building one from scratch. This results in moderate one-time costs for customizing the model since fine-tuning requires computational resources for retraining on your dataset. However, once the model is fine-tuned, the operational costs tend to be lower because you are using an optimized model tailored to your needs, reducing the need for frequent updates or additional training. Fine-tuning strikes a balance between achieving high accuracy in domain-specific tasks and controlling long-term operational costs, making it a cost-effective solution.

Incorrect

High compute costs for retraining the entire model

Fine-tuning only involves adjusting specific layers of a pre-trained model rather than retraining the entire model from scratch. This significantly reduces compute costs compared to training a full model, making this option less applicable to fine-tuning scenarios.

Low initial costs but higher long-term maintenance costs

Fine-tuning involves a moderate initial cost for customization, but it generally leads to lower long-term costs because the model is optimized for your specific use case. Higher long-term maintenance costs are unlikely unless additional fine-tuning is needed regularly.

Increased costs due to the need for large training datasets

Fine-tuning generally requires a smaller, domain-specific dataset compared to training a model from scratch. This reduces the need for large training datasets, minimizing associated data preparation and computational costs.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-foundation-models-fine-tuning.html

questions.text: An organization is using AI for climate research and wants to ensure that the AI model they select aligns with their sustainability goals. They need to minimize the carbon footprint of training and deploying the model. Which of the following should be their primary focus when selecting an AI model?

options.text: Prioritize models trained on the largest dataset available
Select a model that uses minimal computational resources
Focus only on the model with the most advanced features
Use a model that requires frequent retraining to improve accuracy

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Select a model that uses minimal computational resources

To align with sustainability goals, minimizing the carbon footprint of AI models is crucial. AI model training, particularly for large models, can consume significant computational resources, which contributes to increased energy usage and carbon emissions. By selecting a model that uses minimal computational resources, the organization can reduce the environmental impact of both training and deployment. This approach involves optimizing model size, efficiency, and the hardware used for computations. It ensures that the model is eco-friendly while still achieving necessary performance. In the context of AI for climate research, focusing on sustainability requires balancing the capabilities of the model with its environmental impact. Therefore, choosing a model that consumes fewer resources is the most sustainable approach.

Incorrect

Focus only on the model with the most advanced features

While advanced features may provide better performance or insights, they often come at the cost of higher computational requirements, which can increase the carbon footprint. Focusing solely on advanced features without considering resource efficiency is not aligned with sustainability goals.

Prioritize models trained on the largest dataset available

Training on larger datasets typically requires more computation, which increases energy consumption and environmental impact. While larger datasets can improve model accuracy, they are not necessarily the most sustainable option when carbon footprint reduction is a priority.

Use a model that requires frequent retraining to improve accuracy

Frequent retraining increases the computational workload and energy usage, which leads to a higher carbon footprint. Minimizing retraining frequency or optimizing the model to require less retraining is a better strategy for sustainability.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/sustainability

questions.text: A retail company wants to use AI to recommend products to customers based on their previous purchases and browsing history. Which of the following is the best AI use case for this requirement?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Recommendation Systems

Recommendation systems are the best AI solution for recommending products to customers based on their previous purchases and browsing history. These systems analyze past interactions of users (such as purchases, clicks, and browsing behavior) to make personalized product suggestions. Algorithms like collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, or hybrid approaches are commonly used in recommendation systems to predict which items a user might be interested in. This type of AI is widely applied in e-commerce platforms to enhance the customer experience, improve product discovery, and increase sales. By continuously learning from user behavior, recommendation systems can adapt over time, offering increasingly relevant suggestions to customers.

Incorrect

Speech Recognition

Speech recognition focuses on converting spoken language into text. It is used in voice-driven applications, such as virtual assistants, but is not relevant for recommending products based on customer interactions.

Computer Vision

Computer vision deals with analyzing and interpreting visual data, such as images and videos. It is not suitable for tasks like recommending products based on customer purchase history or browsing behavior.

Unsupervised Learning

Unsupervised learning is used to identify patterns or clusters in data without predefined labels. While it can help in understanding customer behavior patterns, it is not specifically tailored for making product recommendations, which usually involve more structured approaches like collaborative filtering.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/tr/blogs/machine-learning/building-a-customized-recommender-system-in-amazon-sagemaker

https://aws.amazon.com/personalize

questions.text: You are developing a recommendation engine for a video streaming platform that needs to store and retrieve embeddings for user preferences and content features. The system requires real-time search capabilities to recommend relevant content based on these embeddings. Which AWS service would you use to store and retrieve embeddings efficiently in this use case?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon OpenSearch Service

Amazon OpenSearch is a fully managed search and analytics service that makes it easy to deploy, operate, and scale OpenSearch clusters in the cloud. It‘s used for a variety of applications like log and event data analysis, real-time monitoring, and website search. OpenSearch allows you to search, visualize, and analyze vast amounts of data quickly and efficiently. It integrates seamlessly with other AWS services and offers advanced features such as machine learning-powered anomaly detection, alerting, and security enhancements. With auto-scaling and easy-to-manage configurations, Amazon OpenSearch reduces the complexity of managing search workloads while ensuring performance and reliability.

Amazon OpenSearch Service (formerly known as Amazon Elasticsearch Service) is the most suitable AWS service for storing and retrieving embeddings efficiently in a real-time search use case, such as a recommendation engine for a video streaming platform. OpenSearch supports vector search, which allows for storing embeddings and performing similarity searches on them. This capability is crucial for recommendation systems that need to match user preferences (represented as embeddings) with content features in real-time.

Incorrect

Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL is a managed relational database service, which excels in structured data queries but is not optimized for real-time search of embeddings or vector-based similarity searches. While it supports extensions like pgvector for vector search, OpenSearch is better suited for large-scale, efficient retrieval of embeddings.

Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

Amazon DocumentDB is a fully managed document database service designed for handling JSON-like documents at scale. It is not optimized for handling vector embeddings or providing real-time search capabilities for recommendation engines. It would require additional workarounds to perform vector searches.

Amazon SageMaker

Amazon SageMaker is a machine learning service for building, training, and deploying models. While SageMaker can help generate embeddings as part of a recommendation engine, it is not a database solution designed for storing or retrieving embeddings. You would still need a separate service, such as Amazon OpenSearch, for efficient embedding storage and retrieval.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/what-is.html

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/amazon-opensearch-services-vector-database-capabilities-explained

questions.text: You are tasked with building an AI-powered recommendation engine using Amazon Bedrock. The recommendation system must efficiently retrieve data and generate responses by leveraging a large knowledge base. You are aware that Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) can enhance the system. What is the primary advantage of using RAG in this context?

options.text: RAG simplifies the training process by minimizing dataset size requirements.
RAG enables real-time inferencing by combining data retrieval with generative capabilities.
RAG improves model accuracy by using supervised learning methods.
RAG reduces the need for model customization by dynamically generating responses.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

RAG enables real-time inferencing by combining data retrieval with generative capabilities.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a method that enhances AI models by integrating real-time data retrieval with generative capabilities. In the context of a recommendation engine using Amazon Bedrock, RAG allows the system to fetch relevant information from a large knowledge base on-the-fly. This means the model doesn‘t rely solely on pre-trained data; instead, it accesses up-to-date information when generating responses. By combining retrieval and generation, RAG enables the recommendation engine to provide timely and contextually accurate suggestions, improving user experience without the need for constant model retraining.

Incorrect

RAG improves model accuracy by using supervised learning methods.

RAG primarily enhances models through real-time data retrieval rather than supervised learning. Supervised learning involves training with labeled data, which is not the main feature of RAG.

RAG reduces the need for model customization by dynamically generating responses.

While RAG does involve dynamic response generation, it doesn‘t eliminate the need for model customization. Customization may still be necessary to tailor the model to specific business needs or domains.

RAG simplifies the training process by minimizing dataset size requirements.

RAG doesn‘t necessarily reduce dataset size requirements for training. Instead, it augments the model‘s capabilities by retrieving external information during inference, not by simplifying the initial training process.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html

questions.text: Your company is deploying an AI solution using Amazon Bedrock, where inference latency is a critical factor. The foundation model will be used for real-time responses in a customer support chatbot. You need to adjust the model‘s inference parameters to optimize for low-latency while maintaining response quality. Which parameter adjustment is most relevant to this scenario?

options.text: Limiting the input/output length to decrease processing time and improve latency.
Allowing the model to process longer sequences to capture more contextual information.
Reducing the model's temperature to ensure more creative responses.
Increasing the model‘s input/output length for detailed responses.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Limiting the input/output length to decrease processing time and improve latency.

When deploying an AI model where inference latency is criticalsuch as a real-time customer support chatbotit‘s essential to optimize the model‘s parameters to reduce response time. Limiting the input and output length is a direct way to decrease the amount of data the model needs to process, which in turn reduces computational load and latency. Shorter inputs mean the model has less information to analyze, and shorter outputs mean it generates responses faster. This adjustment helps maintain an acceptable level of response quality while ensuring that customers receive quick replies, enhancing their overall experience. By carefully selecting the maximum length for inputs and outputs, you can strike a balance between providing sufficient information and achieving low-latency performance.

Incorrect

Increasing the model‘s input/output length for detailed responses.

Increasing input/output length leads to longer processing times, which can worsen latency. While it may provide more detailed responses, it conflicts with the goal of optimizing for low-latency.

Reducing the model's temperature to ensure more creative responses.

Reducing the temperature actually makes the model‘s outputs more deterministic and less random, resulting in less creative responses. Temperature settings affect response variation, not latency.

Allowing the model to process longer sequences to capture more contextual information.

Processing longer sequences increases computational load and latency. While it may improve context understanding, it doesn‘t align with the need for faster responses.

questions.text: You are tasked with building a generative AI model for text translation that needs to handle multiple languages. Which technique will most effectively allow the model to generate translations across different languages?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Multilingual model

A multilingual model is designed to handle and generate text in multiple languages. These models are trained on datasets in different languages, allowing them to perform tasks like translation across a variety of languages effectively. In the context of building a generative AI model for text translation, a multilingual model would be the most appropriate technique.
